simple.meaning: מַעְיָן (maʻyân) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a fountain (also collectively), figuratively, a source (of satisfaction).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 7:11. The surrounding context includes land, mountain.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַעְיָן (H4599) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מַעְיָן (maʻyân) / H4599 is traced through Genesis 7:11, Genesis 8:2, Leviticus 11:36, Joshua 15:9 with generated occurrence evidence.

timeline.evidenceText: In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life, in the second month, on the seventeenth day of the month, on that day all the fountains of the great deep burst open, and the sky’s windows opened.
The deep’s fountains and the sky’s windows were also stopped, and the rain from the sky was restrained.
Nevertheless a spring or a cistern in which water is gathered shall be clean, but that which touches their carcass shall be unclean.
The border extended from the top of the mountain to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, and went out to the cities of Mount Ephron; and the border extended to Baalah (also called Kiriath Jearim);
The south quarter was from the farthest part of Kiriath Jearim. The border went out westward, and went out to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.
Ahab said to Obadiah, “Go through the land, to all the springs of water, and to all the brooks. Perhaps we may find grass and save the horses and mules alive, that we not lose all the animals.”
You shall strike every fortified city, and every choice city, and shall fell every good tree, and stop all springs of water, and mar every good piece of land with stones.’ ”

They beat down the cities; and on every good piece of land each man cast his stone, and filled it. They also stopped all the springs of water, and cut down all the good trees, until in Kir Hareseth all they left was its stones; however the men armed with slings went around it, and attacked it.
So, many people gathered together and they stopped all the springs and the brook that flowed through the middle of the land, saying, “Why should the kings of Assyria come, and find abundant water?”
You opened up spring and stream.
They go from strength to strength.
Those who sing as well as those who dance say,
He sends springs into the valleys.
who turned the rock into a pool of water,
Should your springs overflow in the streets,
When there were no depths, I was born,
Like a muddied spring and a polluted well,
Therefore with joy you will draw water out of the wells of salvation.

definitions.full: H4599. mayan or mayeno or mayanah מַעְיָן noun masculine Prov 8:24 spring ; — absolute ׳מ Psa 74:15 +; construct מַעְיַן 2Kin 3:25 +, מַעְיְנוֺ Psa 114:8 (Ges § 90n ); suffix מַעְיָנוֺ Hosea 13:15 ; plural מַעְיָנוֺת Isa 41:18 +, מַעְיָנִים Psa 104:10 ; construct מַעְיְנוֺת Gen 7:11 +, מַעְיְנֵי 1Kin 18:5 ; 2Kin 3:19 , מַעַיְנֵי Isa 12:3 ; suffix מַעְיָנִי Psa 87:7 (but see below), מַעְיְנֹתֶיךָ Prov 5:16 ; — spring , construct before מַיִם 1Kin 18:5 ; 2Kin 3:19 , 25 ; Josh 15:9 ; 18:15 (both P), Psa 114:8 , compare Prov 8:24 ; ׳מַע alone Isa 41:18 ; Lev 11:36 (P), Psa 74:15 ; 104:10 ; 2Chr 32:4 , compare Joel 4:18 (in eschatological picture); in simile Prov 25:26 ; ׳מ תְּהוֺם Gen 7:11 ; 8:2 (compare Prov 8:28 ); figurative of source of happiness, enjoyment Hosea 13:15 (|| מְקוֺרוֺ Psa 84:7 ; Prov 5:16 (of wife, see Toy), compare ׳מ חָתוּם Song 4:12 , ׳מ גַּנִּים ; 4:15 ; also Psa 87:7 (si vera lectio; so De Che Du; Hup Bae We read form of מָעוֺן dwelling ; ׳מ הַיְשׁוּעָה Isa 12:3 . I. [ עִיף ] = II. עוּף q. v. for עֵיפַי עֵיפָה, etc.
definitions.rootNote: or מַעְיְנוֹ ; (Psalm 114:8), or (feminine) מַעְיָנָה ; from 5869 (as a denominative in the sense of a spring);
